Scientists have used mirrors to test for self-awareness for more than 50 years. 🪞 In a new viral clip, a man holds a mirror up to an AI-powered robot and lets it take in its own reflection. The reaction is wild, and it's already sparking debate over what the machine actually understands. The test dates back to 1970, when psychologist Gordon Gallup Jr. created it to see whether an animal can tell that its reflection is itself. If the subject notices a mark on its own body and reaches for it, that's a sign it recognizes the reflection as itself and not another animal. Robots have passed versions of this before, though at least one was simply programmed to say certain lines when its face-recognition tools spotted itself in the mirror. AI video editor in Claude Code: 3 prompts, from an empty folder to a finished reel. SETUP (once) 1. Get the Claude app (claude.ai/download) and open the Code tab, not the browser. 2. Make a folder "AI Editor" with 3 folders inside: raw, references, done. 3. New chat in Code → Local → Select folder → AI Editor. Needs a paid Claude plan. PROMPT 1: TOOLS You're my video editor. We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here, Python 3.14 or older: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Test each for real: burn a subtitle into a test clip, transcribe 5 seconds of audio. Show a table: tool, version, works or not. PROMPT 2: YOUR TASTE Here are reels whose editing I like: [link 1] [link 2] [link 3]. My format: [talking to camera / voiceover]. Download them with yt-dlp into references (for study only). Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it and ask what to change. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Check cut points by audio level. Keep pauses that serve the meaning, breaths and word endings. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080×1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file yourself, then show me. I'll give edits in plain words; save each as draft-v2, draft-v3. No code words. Follow for my own editing style, coming next.

How to make an animated history short with Claude Code and two free tools - full prompt below. #claudecode #aivideo #history #facelesschannel #aitools What you need: - HyperFrames (free, open source, from HeyGen): github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes - Kokoro voice (open model, 82M parameters, runs on a laptop): github.com/hexgrad/kokoro and huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M - 3 pictures from any image generator Install: 1. In Claude Code: npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes (pick Core Skills) 2. Voice: pip install kokoro soundfile, plus espeak-ng (or ask Claude to install it) The prompt (paste into Claude Code): Make a 45-second vertical history short for a faceless channel. Topic: [one historical event, for example: the Dogger Bank incident, October 1904] 1. Write a 45-second narration script, simple spoken English, with a strong first line. 2. Fact-check it: dates, names, places. Tell me anything you're not sure about. 3. Write prompts for 3 images that match the script. I'll make them and put them in this folder. 4. Check my images against the history: flags, uniforms, ships, maps, the right year. Fix or repaint anything that's wrong and tell me what you changed. 5. Voice the script with Kokoro (voice af_heart) and save the audio. 6. Use HyperFrames to animate the 3 images in layers: slow zoom, pan, parallax, captions in sync with the voice. 7. Render an MP4, 9:16, 1080x1920. Good to know: - HyperFrames Studio has a paid Pro plan. You don't need it to render videos. - Kokoro downloads its model the first time you run it. - Claude checks the facts, but read the script yourself before you post. No code words - everything's right here. Follow for a free AI tool for your content every day.
